new_camps.name: Buck-Berge basin bench camp
new_camps.why: A bench above Buck Creek at the foot of the east ridge: flat ground a short scramble from the start of the climb, so summit day begins fresh and you sleep here both nights.
new_camps.water: Creek and snowmelt in the basin; confirm late in the season.
new_camps.capacity: A few tents on the bench.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness: free self-issue permit at the trailhead; Northwest Forest Pass for parking.
new_camps.notes: Reached by leaving the Buck Creek Trail near the big clearing about 4-6 miles in and bushwhacking up toward the Cleator-Berge area. Most parties base here for the climb and walk out on day 3.

camps.name: Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps
camps.why: Belongs to the Buck Creek side of the peak, not the Napeequa approach this plan uses; only a party switching to the east-side approach would sleep here.

new_camps.name: Treeline camp on Berge's southwest side
new_camps.why: The plan's one camp: flat ground at treeline above the Napeequa that shortens the summit day to a loose scramble, then you drop back and sleep before hiking out.
new_camps.capacity: A few tents on flat spots.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness: free self-issue permit at the trailhead; Northwest Forest Pass for parking.
new_camps.notes: Reached after Little Giant Pass and the Napeequa Valley by a steep intermittent boot track beside the creek. Parties on other Berge routes have camped in larch-dotted bowls around 6,600 ft.

plan_conflict: The camp on file (Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps) serves the Buck Creek approach; this plan's route sleeps at a treeline camp on the southwest side, so it is not slept at here.

new_camps.name: Upper Hook Creek basin camp below The Mole
new_camps.why: Roughly 40 minutes from the base of the north face, so summit day is short and you sleep here again before the walk down.
new_camps.water: Hook Creek and snowmelt in the upper basin.
new_camps.capacity: A handful of tent sites in the basin and on Edward Mesa.
new_camps.permit: Alpine Lakes Wilderness: free self-issue permit at the trailhead.
new_camps.notes: The approach is a brutal, trailless slog of 5,000+ ft through alder and blowdown, so parties carry in and stay put. Ticks have been reported at the sites in early summer.

camps.name: Crescent Lake
camps.why: The natural halfway camp once Mastiff and Howard are behind you: lake water, and it leaves a short morning to the Howard-Rock col and the Rock Mountain summit.

camps.name: Merritt Lake
camps.why: The easy eastern camp with a big site and privy; sleep here only if you start late, then carry over Mastiff and Howard the next morning. Water is scarce east of it.

camps.name: Mount Howard summit-area bivouac
camps.why: A dry crest bivy for sunset and dawn views; you haul water and gear 2,000 ft above Crescent Lake, so it is a choice rather than a plan.

camps.name: Rock Lake
camps.why: Pleasant sites 1.3 miles west of Crescent Lake and close under Rock Mountain; used from the US-2 side or by parties who push past Crescent on day 1.

plan_conflict: The plan puts night 1 in the Upper Canaan Lake basin (about 6,050 ft); no camp by that name is on file and parties are described camping at Crescent Lake, so the plan's camp could not be confirmed.

camps.name: Gardner Meadows
camps.why: End of the Wolf Creek trail among pines with creek water; it puts the tarn and spur ridge to Abernathy's north ridge a half-day from camp.

camps.name: West-side basin camp below Cardinal Peak
camps.why: A meadow near 6,800 ft under the peak: the closest flat camp to the snow approach, so summit day is short and you sleep here both nights.

camps.name: The basin between Emerald and Saska, and Milham Pass
camps.why: A mile and a half past the usual camp, better placed if you are adding Emerald, Saska or the crest traverse; otherwise it is extra carrying.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps.why: Drive-up campgrounds on the long Entiat road; sleep here the night before to start the 9-mile walk in early after the long drive.

camps.name: Fox Camp, North Fork Entiat trail
camps.why: Eight miles in with water by the trail; a gentler day 1 if you are slow, leaving the climb to the following morning.

plan_conflict: The Emerald-Saska basin camp is filed as main on the route page, but the plan sleeps in the basin beneath Cardinal (about 6,800-7,000 ft), so it is demoted to an alternative.

camps.name: Star Lake
camps.why: Larch basin half a mile past Fish Creek Pass with reliable outlet water; the near-universal camp, and it leaves a short, easy walk out the next day.

camps.name: Bird Creek Camp, Devore Creek trail
camps.why: The first workable camp up the Devore Creek trail, about four hours from the lake; parties base here for Devore, Tupshin and Flora and avoid hauling up the brush.

camps.name: The basin between Emerald and Saska, and Milham Pass
camps.why: Larch meadows at 6,800-6,900 ft right beneath the peak; the shared base for Emerald, Saska and Cardinal, so the summit push is short.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps.why: Road campgrounds on the way up the Entiat; sleep here before the walk in to avoid arriving at the trailhead after the long drive.

camps.name: Fox Camp, North Fork Entiat trail
camps.why: A shorter day 1 with water at the trail junction; you then carry up to the basin and its climbs the next morning.

camps.name: The basin between Emerald and Saska, and Milham Pass
camps.why: Meadow camp near 6,800 ft below the peak; one carry in, then Emerald (and often Saska and Cardinal) as light day trips before the walk out.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps.why: Roadside campgrounds in the Entiat valley; useful the night before since the drive in is long and the trail day is big.

camps.name: Fox Camp, North Fork Entiat trail
camps.why: A shorter first day with creek water; the cost is a steeper, longer carry up to the climbing basin the next morning.

camps.name: Cow Creek Meadows
camps.why: Meadow and small lakes with water, about two miles farther than Myrtle Lake but cutting about 1,400 ft off summit day.

camps.name: Larch Lakes meadow camps
camps.why: The highest base, near 5,700 ft, for the shortest summit day; it needs a much longer day 1 carry than the plan describes.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps.why: Car campgrounds near the trailhead; handy the night before for an early start on the gentle river walk.

camps.name: Myrtle Lake
camps.why: The easy half-day camp on the south shore: a short pack in, but it leaves the full 3,950 ft of gain for summit day.

plan_conflict: The Larch Lakes camp is filed as main, but the plan's short day 1 ends at Myrtle Lake or Cow Creek Meadows, so Larch Lakes is not slept at on this plan.

camps.name: Upper Eagle Lake and Horsehead Pass
camps.why: Lakeside sites at 7,110 ft, two hours below the Bigelow finish, with a horse camp and toilet; mosquitoes are heavy at dusk in summer.

camps.name: Eagle Lakes Trail backcountry camp
camps.why: A trail camp about three miles in with a small stream; a shorter first day, but it adds a long summit day with the whole walk out.

new_camps.name: Upper Eagle Lake
new_camps.why: Lakeside camp below the East Face: you can study the cracks from the shore that evening and start the talus to the base at first light.
new_camps.capacity: A horse camp plus four or five tent sites farther along.
new_camps.permit: Northwest Forest Pass for the trailhead; Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness rules apply.
new_camps.notes: The Upper Eagle Lake spur is hard to follow among social trails. Mosquitoes are heavy at dusk in summer; a pit toilet stands at the horse camp.

camps.name: Gardner Meadows, Wolf Creek trail
camps.why: End of the trail with water and flat ground, about 10 miles in; the base most parties use, but it makes for a longer summit day than the high basin.

camps.name: High basin camp above Gardner Meadows
camps.why: A small meadow basin near 6,250 ft that cuts summit-day gain, at the cost of a steep off-trail carry and less certain water.

plan_conflict: The plan sleeps at a high camp in Wolf Creek Basin (about 6,200-6,400 ft), but the route page and other peaks' reports have most parties staying at Gardner Meadows.

camps.name: Oval Lakes basin - West and Middle Oval
camps.why: Middle Oval has the best sites: larch meadows and lake water at the head of the maintained trail, leaving the South Ridge as a half-day light climb.

camps.name: The basin between Emerald and Saska, and Milham Pass
camps.why: The high basin camp near 6,900 ft below Saska Pass; it makes the Saska Pass reclimb the sting in a long summit day, but it is the established camp.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps.why: Road campgrounds in the valley; sleep here the night before so the 9-mile walk in starts early.

camps.name: Fox Camp, North Fork Entiat trail
camps.why: A lower, shorter first day with water at hand; summit day then starts about 1,000 ft lower and is that much longer.

camps.name: Crater Lakes, Crater Creek trail
camps.why: The lake basin at the foot of the southeast ridge, under 4 miles in; early season, tent sites may be snow-covered, so expect to camp on snow.

camps.name: The basin between Emerald and Saska, and Milham Pass
camps.why: Meadow camp at 6,800-7,100 ft beneath the col; summit day is a short light push and you return to the same tents for the second night.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps.why: Road campgrounds on the Entiat; spend the night before here so the long approach day starts early after the drive.

camps.name: Fox Camp, North Fork Entiat trail
camps.why: Eight miles in at the Pyramid trail junction with water; shorter first day, but the carry up to the basin is still waiting.
